_comment: RT-15c (OP-1595) golden wire contract for GET /api/feature-flags/effective. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH shared across the stack: backend/tests/test_feature_flags_dark_ship_e2e.py asserts the REAL endpoint emits these exact payloads, and test/lib/feature-flags-dark-ship-e2e.test.tsx asserts the REAL frontend normalizer/provider/SSR-bootstrap consumes them into the documented UI visibility. If the backend wire shape OR the frontend consumption drifts from these payloads, one side's test goes red. No production/API/provider code is exercised beyond what RT-15a/RT-15b already shipped.

dark.description: Pre-ship dark-ship: no feature_flags row exists for the release-train UI, so the (incomplete) feature ships dark. Every public flag fails closed to false; the UI is invisible to all tenants.

canary.description: Canary reveal: the release-train flag is enabled but scoped to the t-canary allowed_tenants cohort. The dark-shipped UI lights up for the cohort tenant only; every other tenant still sees it dark.

ga.description: General availability: the release-train flag is enabled at rollout_pct=100. The previously dark-shipped UI is now visible to every tenant.

outage.description: Dark-ship safety net: if the flag service / DB is unavailable during GA, the endpoint still returns 200 with every flag false, so the feature safely re-darkens rather than 5xx-ing the page.

leak_guard.description: A hostile/legacy backend response carrying a non-allow-listed key (and a non-boolean value) must be normalized down to the public allow-list as strict booleans before it can reach the UI.
